author: TwinMugsy
body:
So...

Game sort of changes a lot when you hit t10 and t9 to a lesser extent. You will end up unlocking all of the classes if you are playing semi seriously in t10 because you can use the buffs that each class gives to boost whatever class you choose to be your main class. When you unlock classes you can use all of their skills on any class you are currently using. The differences come from the abilities each class has and the stats they give and every one of them has potential to be very potent when well kitted out(pet, gear, amity, ascension levels). Each class has something its sort of the specialist for. A mini breakdown 

Beo relies less on the character and more on the pet usually and can make that pet do silly amounts of damage while often not having to pay a lot of attention once you are buffed

Heratic gets a bonus on crit damage and specializes in magic

Diety is all around and can be built for physical or magical damage while being very tanky

Gilga is super tanky physical that ends up doing more damage for being more tanky

Realmshifter is evasive and physical crit specialist while occasionally getting extra turns

Grand summoner is... well... a summoner. You lose access to using a pet and instead summon things to assist you. Commonly considered the least difficult class to get into end game content although a lot of the things needed for it are event locked which can be frustrating. You dont NEED the event stuff but especially if you are t8 if you get very scary skeleton and buggagane you have a pretty free ride to t10. Even at t10 most summoners have at least 1 VSS on the field at all times for its debuffs

author: Drunkturtle7
body: Beowulf is one of the easiest class to get into t10.  You have many playstyles but the most common is to let your pet do most of the damage. Most basic build is making your character tanky with ward, redlining (having the lowest possible hp to make the most damage), buffing up and setting your ward at 100% absorption. However with celestial classes you get access to 2 more classes, beowulf auriga which focuses on pet damage (pet's may act twice, have better stats and better bonds) and beowulf hydrus (which focuses on hybrid damage like the verse spell) Hydrus is great for pvp, you go all into hybrid stats and damage and use verse which is a great spell since it's elementless and can crit, as a hydrus you also regen hp and mp each time you crit and while your pet is weaker, the act rate is still good enough, which means you now use pets as buff/debuff casters. There's also an off meta build for raiding which involves summoning and using bloodpact. I like the versatility of beowulf.
